categories.claude: Claude.ai, Claude Code and the Anthropic platform

entries.definition: A way of working where suitable AI tools are part of a defined process, not an occasional add-on. Judgement, review and accountability stay clearly assigned to people.
Anthropic's family of AI models. Available models, capabilities, context limits and prices change; check the current provider documentation before you choose.
Anthropic's web interface for Claude. Depending on the current product and plan, it can include Projects, Artifacts, connectors and memory features.
An agentic coding tool with controlled access to files and development tools. Installed and permitted Skills, plugins, MCP servers and subagents can be used.
A workspace in Claude.ai that groups instructions, files and conversations for a defined area of work. How Memory works inside it depends on the current product configuration.
A reusable instruction package for a recurring task. A Skill can combine guidance with permitted tools and supporting resources.
An installable package that can combine Skills, MCP servers, hooks and subagents. Check its contents and permissions before you use it.
An authorised integration between an AI interface and an external source. Available functions, scopes and access rules depend on the provider and configuration.
Model Context Protocol, an open protocol for connecting AI applications to external tools and resources through defined interfaces.
A local or remote service that implements MCP and exposes defined tools or resources. Its security depends on its code, permissions, transport and deployment.
A dedicated Claude.ai view for substantial outputs such as documents, code or visual material. Editing and sharing features depend on the current product.
A frontend-design workflow referenced in this course. It requires explicit visual and interaction decisions before implementation.
Product features that retain selected context across workspaces or conversations. Scope, availability and retention depend on the provider, account and settings.
A Markdown instruction file that Claude Code can load from a project hierarchy. It records project context, conventions and constraints. Keep it current and free of secrets.
A Claude model name referenced by the course material. Check availability, documented capabilities and context limits in the current provider documentation.
A Claude model name referenced by the course material. Select a model against the task, required controls, latency and current provider documentation.
A Claude model name referenced by the course material. Smaller models can suit bounded, high-volume tasks after task-specific evaluation.
Projects, Areas, Resources and Archives: a four-part knowledge-organisation method created by Tiago Forte.
Map of Content: an index note that links a project's material and can record its current status.
A maintained external knowledge system. In this course, it means an Obsidian vault whose notes can be searched and reviewed with supporting tools.
A processing practice in which new notes are reviewed and moved out of the Obsidian inbox at the end of a defined session.
A dated work note used as a scratchpad and link index. It need not be a diary.
An Obsidian community plugin for creating and updating notes from templates.
An Obsidian community plugin for querying metadata and content across a vault.
An Obsidian plugin that can use embeddings to surface semantically related notes. Its data flow depends on the configuration and model provider.
An Obsidian plugin that provides model-assisted chat and retrieval over vault content. Privacy and retention depend on its model and connection settings.
Obsidian's browser extension for saving web content into a vault, with optional processing templates or AI-assisted interpretation.
An MCP integration referenced by the course for exposing an Obsidian vault to Claude Code. Review its code, permissions and network access before using it.
Numerical representations used to compare semantic similarity between items such as passages of text. Their quality and privacy properties depend on the model and pipeline.
A source-available workflow-automation platform with a node-based visual editor and self-hosting options.
The event or schedule that starts a workflow. Common forms include webhooks, schedules, polling and application events.
A workflow step that prepares or performs an operation, such as an API request, review draft or database write. Production use needs permissions, approval and failure handling.
A sequence of triggers, decisions and actions. The course uses simulated patterns; production workflows require versioning, monitoring, access control and recovery paths.
An HTTP endpoint that receives event notifications from another system. Depending on use it needs authentication or signature checks, input validation and replay protection.
Software running on infrastructure the organisation chooses itself. Self-hosting can increase control; on its own it establishes neither security nor GDPR compliance.
A German cloud-hosting provider with data-centre locations in Germany and other regions. Compliance depends on the chosen location, contract and technical configuration.
A desktop application for downloading and running supported language models locally. Hardware needs and data handling vary by model and configuration.
A tool for downloading and running supported models locally through a command-line and local API workflow.
A family of language models developed by Meta. Check each model's licence, size, hardware requirements and intended use before deployment.

Running a model on organisation-controlled hardware instead of sending prompts to a hosted model API. Local execution reduces some data transfers but still requires access control, logging and lifecycle management.
A meeting transcription and note-taking service. Check language support, hosting regions, subprocessors and retention for the plan you choose.
A search product that generates answers with linked sources. Check the original sources yourself before you rely on the answer.
A course model in which a person defines the task and controls while Claude assists with bounded execution. The person reviews and remains accountable for the result.

A legacy course term for structured system use: a clear brief, relevant context, limited permissions and an explicit review step. It does not mean that a model replaces a person or accepts accountability.
One of the course's three basic orchestration patterns: the model produces a first draft and a person edits and approves the next version.
A course pattern in which a model identifies structure, extracts specified fields and returns them in a defined format for review.
A course pattern in which a model organises information against explicit questions and includes sources that a person then verifies.
A briefing structure: Role, Context, Task, Format and Constraints. It works as a checklist for the work and its boundaries.
A prompting term for step-by-step reasoning requests. For a reliable review, ask for concise assumptions, evidence and a verifiable rationale, not private internal reasoning.
Providing a small set of examples before the actual input so the model can follow the demonstrated format or classification rule.
Constraining model output to a defined schema or format such as JSON, CSV or Markdown for validation and downstream processing.

An attack in which untrusted input attempts to override instructions or induce unsafe tool use. Mitigations include separating trusted instructions, limiting permissions, validating inputs and outputs, and requiring approval for consequential actions.
Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, which establishes rules for AI systems in the European Union through a phased application schedule.
Annex III to the EU AI Act lists use cases that may be classified as high-risk when the regulation's conditions and exceptions are met.
An AI system classified as high-risk under the EU AI Act, including qualifying systems covered by Annex I or Annex III. Applicable duties depend on the system, role and use case.

Under the EU AI Act, a person or organisation that develops an AI system or general-purpose AI model, or has one developed, and places it on the market or puts it into service under its own name or trademark.
Under the EU AI Act, a person or organisation using an AI system under its authority, except for personal non-professional use. In a company, the organisation is generally the deployer.
A person or organisation located in the EU that places an AI system bearing the name or trademark of a non-EU entity on the EU market.
Fundamental Rights Impact Assessment. Article 27 of the EU AI Act requires one for specified deployers and qualifying high-risk uses, not for every AI deployment.

Article 4 of the EU AI Act requires providers and deployers to take measures that support the development of AI literacy among staff and other people dealing with AI systems on their behalf. Knowledge, experience, education and training, use context, and affected people or groups must be considered; no specific individual level has to be guaranteed. This course can be one measure among several.
Germany's Act Against Unfair Competition. Section 5 covers misleading commercial practices, including unsupported quantitative claims.
The German abbreviation for the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), which governs processing of personal data in the EU and EEA.
A data processing agreement under GDPR Article 28 between a controller and a processor when the processor handles personal data on the controller's behalf.
GDPR Article 22 concerns certain decisions based solely on automated processing that produce legal or similarly significant effects, subject to its conditions and exceptions.
German administrative principles for keeping and retaining accounting records in electronic form. Applicable retention periods depend on the record type and current law.
A German accreditation and approval regulation for employment-support services. This open course explains the term but makes no funding claim.
Germany's Federal Office for Economic Affairs and Export Control. This open learning platform does not claim a BAFA funding or booking arrangement.
The course's final applied exercise: document and test one bounded workflow, then assess it against a defined rubric.
The free predecessor course to this one. It supports Article 4 AI literacy, data classification and prompting basics, but does not replace a complete internal Article 4 process.
Supporting material covering vault structures, Skill patterns, prompt examples, n8n exercises, MCP guidance and CLAUDE.md starters.
